'''''Crypto: How the Code Rebels Beat the Government Saving Privacy in the Digital Age''''' is a book about [[cryptography]] written by [[Steven Levy]], published in 2001. Levy details the emergence of [[public key]] cryptography, [[digital signatures]] and the struggle between the [[National Security Agency]] and ''[[Cypherpunk#Etymology_and_the_Cypherpunks_mailing_list|cypherpunk]]s''. The book details the creation of [[Data Encryption Standard]] (DES), [[RSA (algorithm)|RSA]] and the [[Clipper chip]].<ref>{{cite news |author=John Naughton |url=https://www.theguardian.com/books/2001/feb/04/computingandthenet.johnnaughton |title=Steven Levy gives a fascinating account of the birth of public key cryptography in Crypto |work=The Guardian |date=February 3, 2001}}<br />- {{cite news |author=Scott McLemee |url=https://www.nytimes.com/books/first/l/levy-crypto.html |title=Decoder Ring — How a ragged band broke the government's hold on cryptography |work=The New York Times |date=January 14, 2001}}</ref>
